title: Annotatio I §.IV: Captivitate Babylonica + Paul — panis is participation; not in pane est
pass_a_gloss: Then in the Book on the Babylonian Captivity: I believe, he says, firmly not only that Christ’s body is in the bread, but that the bread is Christ’s body. For so the Words will keep me, where He says: He took bread, giving thanks broke and said: take, eat. This, i.e. this bread which He had taken and broken, is my body. And Paul: is not the bread which we break a participation of the body of Christ? He does not say (NB.) it is in the bread; but the bread itself is a participation of Christ’s body, and a little later the very usage of speech and common sense proves the subject thus demonstrative of bread (NB.) when He says, this is my body.
pass_b_english: In On the Babylonian Captivity Luther believes not only that Christ’s body is in the bread, but that the bread is Christ’s body — the Words keep him: This = this bread He took and broke.

Paul likewise: the bread we break is participation of Christ’s body — he does not say (NB.) it is in the bread, but the bread itself is that participation; common speech proves the demonstrative subject is bread when He says this is my body.
source_text: Tum in Libro de captivitate Babylonica, Credo inquit, firmiter non modo corpus Christi esse in pane, sed panem esse corpus Christi. Sic enim me servabunt Verba, ubi dicit: accepit panem, gratias agens fregit & dixit: accipite, manducate. Hoc, i. e. hic panis, quem acceperat & fregerat, est corpus meum. Et Paulus, nonne panis quem frangimus participatio corporis Christi est? non dicit (NB.) in pane est; sed ipse panis est participatio corporis Christi, & paulò post ipse usus loquendi & sensus communis probat subjectum sic monstrativum panis (NB.) dum dicit, hoc est corpus meum.
